text:
caro: quick CYI 1 - hit a streaming UX issue while building the generator proxy. when auth refresh happens mid-stream Next() can block for the handshake and handler goroutines hang on client disconnect.

caro: minimal handler that reproduces it:

```go
func proxy(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx := r.Context()
    it := client.NewGenerator("x").Stream(ctx, prompt)
    defer it.Close() // currently Close is only effective after handshake finishes
    for it.Next() {
        if ctx.Err() != nil {
            return
        }
        fmt.Fprint(w, it.Value())
        w.(http.Flusher).Flush()
    }
    if err := it.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("stream error: %v", err) }
}
```

caro: if the token endpoint is slow the library performs a handshake inside Next(), and if the HTTP client disconnects during that handshake our goroutine sits there until auth finishes. tried calling it.Close() in a separate goroutine but that's racy.

teo: thanks for the repro. two simple ergonomics to consider: 1) add Next(ctx) so each blocking call is cancellable and composes with r.Context(), or 2) make Close() cancel the in-flight handshake immediately (so Next() unblocks).

mina: I'm strongly in favor of Next(ctx) for HTTP handlers. usage is clear:

for it.Next(r.Context()) {
    io.WriteString(w, it.Value())
}

mina: also recommend surface ErrCanceled (or reuse context.Canceled) so callers can distinguish a client abort from an auth/network error.

teo: agree re: ErrCanceled. Implementation detail: the auth refresh path must accept a context and return early with context.Canceled if the caller cancels. otherwise Next(ctx) won't help.

caro: noted. i'll prototype a small change where Next(ctx) is introduced and internal handshake/token refresh accepts a ctx. i can keep Stream(ctx) for parity but mark it as less robust for handler patterns.

mina: tests: add an httptest.Server + fake auth that sleeps on refresh. the test should close the client connection after ~30ms while auth sleeps 200ms and assert the server-side goroutine exits within the test timeout. that will catch leaks.

ops-bot: FYI flaky-test detector: we have a test harness that kills tests stuck > 500ms, but this one was subtle and escaped detection. adding the explicit assert will help.

caro: good call. i'll add the failing test first so CI shows the regression locally, then implement Next(ctx) + cancellable refresh.

ci-bot: Created PR #4357: "go: generator iterator Next(ctx) + cancellable auth refresh + ErrCanceled" 1 reviewers: @mina @teo

caro: thanks all. if anyone has a concise helper to simulate client disconnects in httptest (without pulling in heavy deps) drop it here; otherwise i'll attach the proxy sample and the deterministic test to the PR.
